title: In the Future, 200,000 Employees Will Collaborate with 20 Million AI Agents; Microsoft Has Developed a Dedicated Management System for Them

content_html:
With artificial intelligence technology booming, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella recently shared his grand vision for the future shape of corporate organizations and human-AI collaboration on the podcast “Possible,” hosted by LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, sparking widespread discussion in the tech world.

A Future Beyond Imagination: 20 Million Agents Working Alongside 200,000 Employees

On the podcast, Nadella put forward a highly disruptive hypothesis: "What if, in the future, we had 200,000 employees and also 2 million, or even 20 million, agents participating in the work? What would that look like?"

He compared this future trend of humans and AI working together to the situation in the 1980s. At the time, no one would have believed that in future offices, billions of people would sit in front of computers typing on keyboards every day. In Nadella's view, AI is by no means just an isolated technology tool; it will completely reshape and become the core foundation of future enterprises.

Programming Evolution and Hands-On Experience: Personally Testing 100 Agents Running at Once

Looking back at the trajectory of AI, Nadella pointed out that the evolution of programming clearly foreshadows the future direction of all work: from early code autocompletion, to chatbots, to agents handling simple tasks, and ultimately to advanced agents that can run autonomously for long periods. In this model, users can even launch tasks directly and then no longer need human intervention.

To experience this change firsthand, Nadella revealed that he had tried opening 100 CLI sessions at once and running 100 different agents in parallel. However, as the number of agents increases exponentially, the cognitive burden of managing them also rises. For this reason, Microsoft has developed a dedicated "agent development environment" system for him internally, to efficiently manage and orchestrate these massive numbers of AI agents.
